children: Genmab shares climbed after the Danish biotech said an experimental drug cut the risk of death and disease progression for ovarian-cancer patients in a late-stage clinical trial.
Shares in Genmab were up 13% in European morning trade Monday, lifting their year-to-date gain to nearly 48%.

The company said late Friday that its rinatabart sesutecan, or Rina-S, drug candidate met its primary and key secondary goals in the late-stage clinical trial by cutting the risk of death by 57% and of disease progression by 71%, compared to chemotherapy, in patients with an advanced form of ovarian cancer.
These were the first late-stage study results for the drug and strengthen Genmab's confidence in its potential, the company's chief executive, Jan van de Winkel, said.

The unprecedented efficacy for Rina-S together with the recent success for lymphoma drug Epkinly and expectations of positive data for a third drug, petosemtamab, in a late-stage trial in head and neck cancer should improve investors' confidence in Genmab's growth prospects, analysts at J.P. Morgan wrote in a note to clients.
Genmab also released follow-up data over the weekend from a midstage trial of petosemtamab in colorectal cancer that the company said pointed to promising depth and durability of response.

title: Genmab Shares Jump After Positive Cancer Study Results
